changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6681-declared-lazy-marketplace-routes.md`

- names `views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Both marketplace chunks were held by CHUNK CO-TENANCY, not by any import of the page: rolldown had parked `components/SuggestedBindingsPanel.tsx` (statically imported by the eager `views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx`) in the first, and `console/marketplace/InstalledListWidget.tsx` (bare-imported by the package barrel for its SDUI registration) in the second. An `app-shell-eager-leaves` group in `apps/console/vite.config.ts` isolates those co-tenants so the three declared-lazy pages chunk by their own dynamic-only reachability. The console eager closure moves 3180.2 KB → 3171.5 KB gzipped (−8,888 bytes, 48 → 45 eager chunks) with the three per-chunk ceilings unmoved.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `e978ed5ea` (merge-base with origin/main): 2 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1794 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2401 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36690115887)

Those conclusions are the gate verdicts here; the dev's own gate readings in `5907370098` are consistent with them and not re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Binding direction (triage `5903144429`): close nav editing on the transition to read-only; keep the toggle ungated while writability is unknown; one writer through the same `readOnly` flag; pins for the in-flight then `writable: false` close with nothing left unsaved on screen, and the `writable: true` control.

1. **The effect, keyed on `readOnly`, `editNav` and `navDirty` (head `:1652`–`:1662`).** Right. It is a no-op while `readOnly` is false, and while `readOnly` holds neither of the other two keys can become true: the toggle renders under `!readOnly` (`:2551`), the deep link's apply enters editing only with `enterEditing: readOnly === false` (hook `:96`), and `setNavDirty(true)` has exactly one writer, `onNavPatch` (`:2069`), whose two consumers, `AppNavCanvas` (`:2613`) and `StudioNavItemInspector` (`:2333`, `:2339`), render only under `editNav`. So the extra keys only ever re-run it as a no-op after the close; it cannot fire on a read-only package that has nothing open, and it cannot clear a read-only deep-link selection, because `setNavSel(null)` sits under `if (editNav)`. Keying on `readOnly` alone would have read `editNav` and `navDirty` from the closure with the same result on the transition render; the chosen shape is the lint-clean one. Deviation 4 answered: right.
2. **Matches the toggle's close path.** Right. The toggle flips `editNav` and calls `setNavSel(null)` (`:2555`–`:2556`) and nothing else; the effect is `setEditNav(false); setNavSel(null)`. The nav-item inspector renders on `editNav && navSel` (`:2333`) and closes with them. Pin 4 covers the inspector.
3. **The put-back (dirty buffer to `navBaselineRef`, `navDirty` cleared): discarding is right.** The card's pin says "no edit is left on screen unsaved", and the rail's view-mode `NavTree` renders `navTree`, which is derived from `appDraft.navigation` (`:1620`), the same object that is the edit buffer. A kept dirty buffer would show the refused item in view mode as if it were the package's navigation, and hold `navDirty` for good: the leave guard mirror (`:1693`) and the copilot refresh hold (`useMetadataRefreshNonce(navDirty || !!navSaving)`, `:1710`) both key on it, and nothing on a read-only package can ever clear it, since the nav autosave is `blocked: … || readOnly` (`:2104`) and the package list is only re-asked on a package switch, which rehydrates the buffer anyway. The baseline is sound: `setAppDraft` has exactly four writers, the declaration, the load (`:1894`, baseline written beside it `:1895`), `onNavPatch` (the dirtying one) and this effect; `doNavSave` records the document it sent only AFTER the await (`:2091`), so a save the server refuses (the "debounce ran out while unknown" case) leaves the baseline at the last load and its `setNavDirty(false)` unreached, and the effect then puts back and clears. Deviation 3 answered: the divergence from the toggle is required by the card's own wording, and the PR body states why.
4. **Declaration order before `useNavSelDeepLink`.** Right, and necessary. The effect is declared at `:1652`, the hook call at `:1673`; React runs a component's effects in declaration order, so on the render where `readOnly` flips true and the hook's `settled` flips true (`readOnlySettled ? readOnly : undefined`, `:1677`) the close's `setNavSel(null)` is queued before the apply's `setNavSel(hit)`, and the batch ends on the link's selection. Ablation leg 2 (effect moved after the hook: only pin 3 red, on `selParam()`) matches that mechanism. One residual, outside the card's pins and not a defect this card owes: the apply resolves the link's spec id to a POSITIONAL selection against the render's `navDoc`, which is still the dirty document, and the put-back in the same commit then re-points it. An "Add nav item" appends, so pin 3 holds; a drag-reorder or an insert before the linked item inside the in-flight window would leave the mirror writing another item's id, or deleting `sel`. URL-only, no edit involved, an edge of the edge; noted for the seat in ③.
5. **The race-pin file is byte-unchanged.** Confirmed by content: `contents/…/StudioDesignSurface.navDeepLink-11153.test.tsx` has the same blob sha `6f15404de902a0e762b42d9333127592eb7b125b` (12621 bytes) at the head and at `main`. It is not in the PR's file list.
6. **Five pins and two ablation legs.** The five cases are the card's two pins plus three the dev owes for the mechanism: (1) whole surface, in flight, item added, `writable: false`: toggle hidden, canvas gone, "Done editing" absent, the loaded items shown and "New item" nowhere, leave guard released; (2) the control, `writable: true`: editing open, item on screen, save reached and read back after the re-read; (3) a pending `?sel=nav:nav_landing` link survives the close; (4) pillar level, a link that opened editing, re-rendered `readOnly`: editing and the linked item's inspector close; (5) the writable re-render control. Each read-only case has its control, and the control proves the edit is real (it reaches a save). Leg 1 (effect deleted: 3 red, the three read-only pins, on `navEditingOpen()`) is the card's defect reproduced; leg 2 is the ordering. Both restores proven by blob. The second commit fixed the harness's served-draft envelope so the control no longer depends on timing; that is a test-only change. The harness mocks `./packages-io` and `../metadata-admin/useMetadata`, both real imports of the subject (`:140`, `:96`); the Inert vi.mock Specifier Check on the head is green.
7. **Confined to `InterfacesPillar`.** Right. `InterfacesPillar` spans `:1556`–`:2814`; every source hunk (the `navBaselineRef` and moved `navDirty` declarations, the effect, the load's baseline write, the save's baseline write) lies inside it. `navDirty`'s `useState` moved above the effect; hook order is the same on every render, so that is inert. No prop, no export, no other pillar, no shared hook moved.
8. **Public surface / accept-set.** None moves. `InterfacesPillar`'s props are unchanged; the nav document's shape is unchanged; the deep-link hook is untouched; no schema, string or route is added. The one behaviour that changes is the read-only transition inside the pillar.

1. **PR assignee not written**, the `label-write.mjs --assign` refused by the auto-mode classifier. Noted only, as the brief directs: `pulls/11187` shows `assignee: null`; it is not a gate and this record does not re-route it.

3. **The buffer put-back diverging from the toggle.** Answered in ① item 3: right, and required by the card's "no edit is left on screen unsaved".
4. **Three-key effect rather than `readOnly` alone.** Answered in ① item 1: right.

`open_questions`: none declared; none found.

Out-of-scope notes:
- **Two class-a findings, the objectui#11124 / objectui#11136 family, both in `InterfacesPillar`'s nav autosave.** (1) "Done" inside the 1.5 s debounce: the nav autosave is `blocked: … || !editNav` (`:2104`), so the pending timer is cleared, `navDirty` stays true, and the edit sits in the view-mode tree with the leave guard held until editing is reopened (then the autosave re-arms). (2) an Add while a save is in flight: `doNavSave` runs `setNavDirty(false)` after its await regardless of edits taken meanwhile (`:2093`), and the `onDraftSaved` re-read installs the served draft over the buffer (`:2094`, load `:1894`), so the second edit is shown and then silently dropped. Judgment: ONE family closure card, not two. Same site (the nav autosave's dirty/blocked/save wiring in one pillar), same class (an editor that takes an edit its autosave does not send), and one fix surface (a flush on Done, and a dirty generation so a completing save clears only what it sent and the re-read does not overwrite a dirty buffer), carried as two pins. Both are measured in an uncommitted happy-dom probe, not a live browser; (2) is the graver, being an outright loss, not a deferral. Whether an existing family closure card already carries them is the seat's dedupe, outside this record's inputs. Not in this PR's scope, and rightly so: the card's site is the read-only transition.
- **No notice on the put-back** (carrier: none). Accepted as a residual, not a defect: the discarded edit was taken inside the package-list window, the author sees the toggle vanish and the canvas close, and Publish carries the read-only hint; a toast needs strings in every locale pack, outside this card's file surface. If the seat wants a notice, it is its own small card, and the same card could carry ① item 4's URL residual (a pending link's positional selection resolved against the pre-put-back document).
